title: Bootstrap architecture foundation
body:
## Outcome

The Basecamp repository has the initial monorepo skeleton, product architecture, data model, Kaizen UI strategy, seed content, and CI repository check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Monorepo structure exists.
- Product architecture is documented.
- Seed content exists as structured data.
- CI repository check passes.

## Validation

- `pnpm check` passes.

## Release

- v0.1.0

title: Establish GitHub roadmap, milestones, issues, and release plan
body:
## Outcome

GitHub becomes the live planning system for Basecamp so the next work is visible through issues, milestones, and releases.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Roadmap document exists.
- GitHub planning workflow is documented.
- Release process is documented.
- Milestone and issue seed data exists.
- Roadmap sync script exists.

## Validation

- `pnpm check` passes.

## Release

- v0.1.0

title: Define initial TypeScript domain model package
body:
## Outcome

`@basecamp/domain` exports the first typed model for categories, levels, quests, accomplishments, inventory references, evidence references, and maintenance references.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Domain types cover the seed dataset concepts.
- Types distinguish owned, configured, tested, validated, and maintained states.
- User-controlled pursuit states are represented.
- Type examples or fixtures exist.

## Validation

- Type checks pass.
- Seed data can be mapped into domain types.

title: Add structured content validation for seed data
body:
## Outcome

Seed content is validated beyond basic JSON parsing so broken quests, categories, levels, dependencies, badges, capability outposts, and milestones fail CI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Validator checks IDs, references, duplicate IDs, required fields, and dependency targets.
- Validator checks quests have validation criteria.
- Validator runs through `pnpm check`.
- Errors are readable for content authors.

## Validation

- Add at least one fixture or targeted test for invalid content.

title: Select web and server framework stack ADR
body:
## Outcome

The first running stack is chosen intentionally instead of by habit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ADR evaluates Next.js, Vite plus Fastify, Remix, and server-only alternatives.
- Recommendation covers Kaizen compatibility, self-hosting, local network use, mobile sync, testing, and deployment complexity.
- Migration path is documented.

## Validation

- ADR is linked from architecture docs.

title: Implement server health and seed content API
body:
## Outcome

`apps/server` exposes a minimal API that proves the server can start and serve structured Basecamp seed content.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Health endpoint exists.
- Seed categories, levels, and quests can be read through a typed API.
- API contracts live in or flow through `@basecamp/api`.
- No UI feature depends on raw content JSON paths.

## Validation

- Server test or smoke check passes.

title: Implement web shell and dashboard skeleton
body:
## Outcome

`apps/web` starts locally and renders the first Basecamp dashboard shell using the approved UI boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Web app starts with documented command.
- Dashboard shell shows Readiness Score placeholder, category levels, active quests, recommended next, and maintenance placeholder.
- Feature code imports from `@basecamp/ui` rather than Kaizen directly.
- Basic keyboard and semantic structure are present.

## Validation

- Local smoke check or web test confirms the dashboard route renders.

title: Build initial Basecamp UI Kaizen adapter spike
body:
## Outcome

`@basecamp/ui` proves the Kaizen adapter boundary with a small set of real components and documented rules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Initial components include Button, Card or Panel, StatusBadge, ProgressRing or equivalent, and PageShell.
- Kaizen direct imports are isolated to `packages/ui`.
- CSS/token strategy is documented after inspecting installed package assets.
- Accessibility defaults are described.

## Validation

- Component exports can be imported by `apps/web`.

title: Add database tool decision and first migration baseline
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp has a chosen database migration/query approach and the first schema baseline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ADR evaluates Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely, and SQL migration alternatives.
- Initial migration covers categories, levels, quest templates, and seed import tracking.
- Local database setup is documented.

## Validation

- Migration can be applied from a clean local database.

title: Add seed import workflow
body:
## Outcome

Structured seed content can be imported into the local development database in a repeatable way.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Import command exists.
- Import is idempotent for stable IDs.
- Imported content version is recorded.
- Clear error messages are produced for invalid content.

## Validation

- Clean import and repeated import both pass.

title: Add vertical-slice smoke test
body:
## Outcome

CI can prove the first web/server/content slice still works.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Smoke test starts or exercises the server and web shell as appropriate.
- Test confirms categories and quests render or are reachable.
- Test runs from `pnpm check` or a documented CI job.

## Validation

- CI passes with the new smoke check.

title: Document local developer setup for the running slice
body:
## Outcome

A developer can clone the repo, install dependencies, run checks, and start the first app without asking what to do next.

## Acceptance Criteria

- README quickstart is updated.
- Required runtime versions are explicit.
- Database setup is documented if introduced.
- Common troubleshooting notes are included.

## Validation

- Follow docs from a clean checkout or fresh local environment.

title: Implement quest lifecycle and active backlog model
body:
## Outcome

Users can start, save, pause, resume, snooze, abandon, complete, and reopen quests without Basecamp forcing a single path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Quest statuses are modeled and persisted.
- Multiple active quests are supported.
- Saved and deferred quest lists are supported.
- User actions are auditable enough for future sync.

## Validation

- Unit tests cover lifecycle transitions.

title: Implement category progression paths
body:
## Outcome

Each category can display a progression path with levels, nodes, node states, and accessible fallback navigation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Path nodes represent accomplishments, skills, builds, tests, drills, milestones, and capability outposts.
- Node states include completed, current, available, locked, deferred, failed validation, and maintenance required.
- Keyboard/screen-reader usable list representation exists.

## Validation

- Tests or story fixtures cover core node states.

title: Implement dependency graph resolver
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp can lock specific dependent work without locking unrelated preparedness activities.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dependency types include knowledge, skill, equipment, supply, tool, machinery, drill, validation, and optional recommendation.
- Resolver explains why an item is locked or available.
- Resolver handles missing dependencies gracefully.

## Validation

- Unit tests cover available, locked, and unrelated unlocked paths.

title: Implement readiness score v1
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp calculates initial category and overall readiness scores that distinguish owning gear from validated capability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Category score includes knowledge, supplies/equipment, configuration, practice, validation, maintenance, and redundancy weights.
- Overall score identifies critical gaps.
- Validation ceilings prevent purchase-only high scores.
- Deferred categories are visible without being treated as errors.

## Validation

- Unit tests cover purchase-only, configured, tested, validated, and maintenance-stale cases.

title: Implement recommendation engine v1
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp recommends a small set of useful next choices while preserving user control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Recommendations consider probability, consequence, capability gap, dependency importance, friction, user interests, deferred categories, downstream unlocks, and quick wins.
- Output can show best risk reduction, quick win, build project, skill, drill, or maintenance.
- Recommendation does not automatically activate a quest.

## Validation

- Tests cover deferred category suppression and quick-win ranking.

title: Implement XP, badge, capability outpost, and milestone progress v1
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp tracks motivational progress without confusing XP with readiness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- XP events are recorded with source and reason.
- Badge tier progress can be calculated from seed definitions.
- Capability outpost and milestone requirements can be evaluated.
- Purchase-only actions earn limited XP.

## Validation

- Tests cover badge progress and capability outpost requirement evaluation.

title: Implement category hold and defer controls
body:
## Outcome

Users can intentionally hold a completed level or defer a category without Basecamp repeatedly pushing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Category pursuit states are user-editable.
- Recommendation engine respects later, paused, and not currently pursuing states.
- Dashboard still shows gaps clearly.

## Validation

- Tests cover recommendation suppression for deferred categories.

title: Implement inventory, location progression, assets, kits, and QR tag data model
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp can represent consumables, durable assets, user-named locations, location progression, kits/loadouts, and Basecamp QR asset tags.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Model covers inventory items, lots, assets, locations, location hierarchy, location readiness, kits, kit items, and asset tags.
- Locations can be named by the user and can progress independently from known location to stash, outpost, basecamp, and home base.
- Multiple locations can reach home base maturity.
- Physical outpost locations are distinct from, but linkable to, gamified category capability outpost achievements.
- States include owned, located, installed, configured, tested, in service, maintenance due, failed, retired, and expired.
- Inventory events are modeled rather than only overwriting totals.

## Validation

- Migration and model tests cover core inventory scenarios and location progression scenarios.

title: Implement BOM and acquisition rollup v1
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp can derive what the user needs to buy, make, build, replenish, or substitute from active quests and BOMs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- BOM items include functional requirement, quantity, specification, required/optional state, cost, replacement interval, and alternatives.
- Acquisition needs are derived from active quests and inventory.
- User does not manually maintain a separate shopping list.

## Validation

- Tests cover already owned, need to purchase, need to make, optional, and substitute cases.

title: Implement recurring maintenance policies and completion events
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp tracks recurring maintenance and lets normal completion happen with approximately one interaction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Maintenance policies define recurrence and scope.
- Completion events recalculate next due date.
- Failure or issue events can create suggested follow-up quests.
- Dashboard can show upcoming and overdue maintenance.

## Validation

- Tests cover next due calculation and failure follow-up creation.

title: Implement web quick inventory entry flow
body:
## Outcome

Users can add common inventory without long forms.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Search-first flow supports item, quantity, location, expiration if relevant, and notes.
- Smart defaults reduce fields.
- Added inventory updates relevant quest/BOM progress.
- Bulk entry path is considered for common supplies.

## Validation

- Manual workflow count is documented for the implemented flow.

title: Design and implement QR asset tag generation
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp can generate QR tags for assets such as radios, generators, batteries, bins, kits, fuel containers, and tools.

## Acceptance Criteria

- QR code maps to a stable Basecamp asset identifier.
- Printed tag layout is usable.
- Scanning a tag can open the asset workflow.
- Offline/local network behavior is documented.

## Validation

- QR generation and lookup are tested or manually verified.

title: Implement mobile app foundation
body:
## Outcome

`apps/mobile` starts as a real mobile companion app with navigation for Home, Capture, Scan, Quests, Inventory, and Offline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Mobile stack ADR is finalized.
- App shell runs locally.
- Shared domain/API packages are consumable.
- Mobile design-system boundary is documented.
- iPhone installation documentation is updated for the chosen distribution path and does not require normal users to build from source.
- Documentation covers minimum supported iOS version, install channel, server URL setup, pairing/sign-in, iOS permissions, first sync, offline verification, updates, and lost/replaced device removal.
- Mobile test instructions identify which checks may run in a simulator and which require a physical iPhone.

## Validation

- Mobile app starts in local simulator or documented environment.
- iPhone installation instructions are followed on a device or explicitly marked as pending until TestFlight or stable distribution exists.
- Resolution comment records whether validation used a simulator, physical iPhone, local machine, or separate server.

title: Implement Quick Capture command parser v1
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp can turn natural entries like `Bought four gallons of water` or `Changed generator oil` into confirmation cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Deterministic parser handles inventory, maintenance, drill, skill, failure, and quest progress examples.
- Parser produces a user-confirmable command.
- No SaaS AI dependency is required for normal operation.

## Validation

- Tests cover the core examples from the product brief.

title: Implement barcode and QR scanning mobile workflows
body:
## Outcome

Mobile scanning reduces inventory and asset maintenance friction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Barcode scan can create or update an inventory confirmation flow.
- QR scan opens the matching Basecamp asset.
- Asset actions include inspect, maintain, move, adjust quantity, report issue, and view instructions where supported.
- Offline behavior is defined.
- Physical iPhone test instructions cover camera permission, QR scan, barcode scan, local network behavior, offline behavior, and expected pass/fail notes.

## Validation

- Scanner workflow is manually verified on a physical iPhone when camera behavior is in scope.
- Simulator validation is acceptable only for non-camera layout or routing checks.

title: Implement offline read model and command outbox
body:
## Outcome

Mobile can keep critical information available offline and queue field actions for later sync.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Offline read model includes active quests, inventory, plans, critical BOMs, maintenance, and references.
- Command outbox is durable.
- Commands include client ID, local sequence, timestamp, entity version, and intent.
- Physical iPhone test instructions cover first sync, airplane-mode/offline access, queued changes, reconnect, and sync confirmation.

## Validation

- Tests cover queued commands and retry behavior.
- Offline and reconnect behavior is verified on a physical iPhone or explicitly deferred with a follow-up issue until mobile distribution exists.

title: Implement sync API v1 and conflict policies
body:
## Outcome

The server can accept idempotent offline commands, return sync cursors, and resolve common conflicts predictably.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Sync endpoint accepts command batches.
- Server validates command identity and idempotency.
- Merge policies exist for inventory quantity events, maintenance events, quest status, and evidence.
- User-visible conflicts are modeled.
- Test instructions cover local-machine server validation and separate-server validation when admin access is provided.

## Validation

- Sync tests cover duplicate commands, clean replay, and at least two conflict types.
- Resolution comment records whether sync validation ran locally, against a separate server, or both.

title: Implement drill templates, runs, and follow-up quests
body:
## Outcome

Users can run structured drills, record lightweight results, and turn failures into improvement quests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Drill templates include scenario and success criteria.
- Drill runs capture result, failures, lessons, evidence, and follow-up actions.
- Failed criteria can create suggested quests.
- Drill completion affects readiness validation.

## Validation

- Tests cover drill success and failed-drill follow-up generation.

title: Implement skill progression and training records
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp tracks skills independently from equipment and uses practice/training evidence in readiness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Skill states include untrained, familiar, practiced, competent, validated, and advanced.
- Training records can include course, date, expiration, and evidence.
- Skills can satisfy dependencies and contribute to scoring.

## Validation

- Tests cover skill state progression and expiration impact.

title: Implement evidence and photo capture model
body:
## Outcome

Evidence supports validation without making the user write long reports.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Evidence can link to quests, accomplishments, skills, drills, assets, maintenance, and inventory events.
- Photo/document metadata is modeled.
- Offline upload retry behavior is considered.
- Evidence deletion/versioning policy is documented.

## Validation

- Tests or fixtures cover evidence links to multiple entity types.

title: Implement validation ceilings in readiness scoring
body:
## Outcome

Readiness scores cannot rise unrealistically from untested owned gear.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each relevant category has a validation ceiling rule.
- Purchase-only, configured-only, and validated states produce meaningfully different scores.
- Drill failure can reduce or cap readiness until follow-up work is done.

## Validation

- Tests cover score caps and recovery after validation.

title: Implement reports and gap analysis v1
body:
## Outcome

Users can see critical gaps, deferred areas, validation gaps, maintenance issues, and next useful choices.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Report identifies critical category gaps.
- Report distinguishes intentional deferral from unknown gaps.
- Report shows validation gaps separately from acquisition gaps.
- Report can suggest follow-up quests.

## Validation

- Fixture profile produces expected report sections.

title: Implement Docker Compose self-hosting baseline
body:
## Outcome

A user can run Basecamp on a Linux host with documented container services.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Compose file includes web, server, database, storage path, and reverse proxy or documented proxy option.
- Persistent volumes are defined.
- Environment configuration is documented with safe defaults.
- Deployment guide covers host prerequisites, admin-controlled paths, release artifact download, configuration, startup, migrations, health checks, browser access, remote access stance, backup setup, restore drill, and troubleshooting.
- Separate-server validation instructions cover the access facts needed from the admin, rollback/cleanup, and how success is reported.
- Local network operation does not require internet after setup.

## Validation

- Fresh compose deployment starts and health checks pass.
- Deployment guide is followed from a fresh host, clean VM, or separate server provided by the admin.
- Resolution comment records which environment was used.

title: Implement backup and restore automation
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp can be backed up and restored with confidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Backup includes database, evidence files, config, version, and seed/content version.
- Restore procedure is documented.
- Backup integrity check exists.
- Stale or failed backup status can be surfaced.

## Validation

- Restore drill succeeds from a fresh deployment.

title: Implement release packaging and upgrade process
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp releases are installable, upgradeable, and understandable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Release checklist is implemented in docs and scripts where useful.
- Server/web install steps are included or linked from each installable release.
- Mobile install steps are included or linked once mobile distribution exists.
- Upgrade steps cover migrations and backup-before-upgrade.
- Release notes include known limitations and validation environment.
- Rollback guidance is documented.

## Validation

- Dry-run release process is documented or tested.
- Release notes link to current deployment and mobile installation guides where applicable.
- Release notes say whether validation ran locally, on a clean local environment, on a separate server, in a simulator, or on a physical iPhone.

title: Implement security hardening baseline
body:
## Outcome

Basecamp has a sensible self-hosted security baseline for sensitive preparedness data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Authentication and authorization approach is documented and implemented for beta needs.
- Secrets are kept out of git and documented through env/config files.
- Export, backup, admin, and restore actions are audited.
- Remote access guidance favors VPN or secure reverse proxy patterns.

## Validation

- Security checklist passes for beta deployment.

title: Implement health checks and observability baseline
body:
## Outcome

The self-hosted deployment exposes enough health information to operate safely.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Health endpoints cover web, server, database, storage, migrations, and backup recency.
- Logs are useful without exposing sensitive data.
- Basic operational dashboard or status endpoint is available.

## Validation

- Compose health checks pass and fail clearly when dependencies are unavailable.

title: Implement data export and import baseline
body:
## Outcome

Users retain ownership of Basecamp data and can export/import it in useful formats.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Structured JSON export exists.
- CSV exports exist for major operational data where useful.
- Evidence files are included or referenced in a portable archive.
- Import validates version compatibility.

## Validation

- Export from one local deployment can be imported into another.

title: Define v1.0 MVP readiness criteria
body:
## Outcome

The team has an explicit, testable definition for when Basecamp is a real MVP instead of an endless prototype.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Required web workflows are listed.
- Required mobile workflows are listed.
- Required offline/sync behavior is listed.
- Required self-hosting and backup behavior is listed.
- Required server/web deployment instructions are listed.
- Required iPhone mobile installation instructions are listed.
- Required validation environments are listed, including local machine, clean local environment, separate server, simulator, and physical iPhone where appropriate.
- Required Compose config validation is listed, including `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --env-file infra/basecamp.env.example config --quiet`.
- Required proof that backup/restore covers database, storage, and admin configuration is listed.
- Required content coverage and validation behavior are listed.
- Non-goals for v1.0 are listed.

## Validation

- v1.0 readiness checklist is linked from the roadmap and release docs.
